title: Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (MGySgt to SSgt) NMOS (6842), DC I
raw_text:
4. MOS 6877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (MGySgt to SSgt)
NMOS (6842), DC I

    a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Meteorology and Oceanography
(METOC) Forecasters train personnel on environmental characterization and
effects in relation to aviation operations in support of the MAGTF and



                                         3-437                          Enclosure (1)
 3145                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



aviation ground equipment, sensor, and weapon system performance in relation
to enemy threats. WTI METOC Forecasters are proficient in the development of
environmental sensing plans to characterize the physical environment and
operational orders development required for designated staff billets. This
MOS is assigned only as an NMOS to qualified METOC Forecasters.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 6842.

            (2) Must complete aviation career progression model (ACPM) via Marine
Net:

                (a) MAWTS8000X ACPM-8000 MACCS.

                (b) MAWTS8020X ACPM-8020 ACE.

                (c) MAWTS8040X ACPM-8040 Threat.

                (d) MAWTS8060X ACPM-8060 MAGTF.

                (e) MAWTS8080X ACPM-8080 Joint Air Operations.

        (3) Must hold the senior instructor (SI) designation per the MAWTS-1
Command, Control, and Communication (C3) Course Catalog.

        (4) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and
Tactics Instructor Course (M149721) Yuma, AZ.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Management of local or subordinate METOC technical training
programs.

        (2) Identify technical training shortfalls that prevent or hinder the
development of METOC products in support of decision makers.

        (3) Develop or assist in the development of technical training that
improves METOC support to decision makers.

        (4) Identify new or emerging METOC doctrinal support methods through
Marine Corps Lesson Learned.

        (5) Develop or assist in the development of new METOC Tactics,
Techniques & Procedures (TTPs) from Marine Corps Lessons Learned.

        (6) Develop the Annex H of a MAGTF or MSC operational order or plan
to support Marine Corps, Joint, or Coalition operations in support of
contingencies.

        (7) Develop MAGTF environmental collection plans that integrate with
Joint Coalition environmental sensing strategies to support Marine Corps
operations in support of contingencies.




                                        3-438                        Enclosure (1)
 3145                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (8) Identify METOC sensitivities for MAGTF systems and operations to
establish METOC thresholds to support all elements of the MAGTF by
understanding the impact of the physical environment.

        (9) Identify METOC sensitivities for enemy systems and operations to
establish METOC thresholds to determine opportunities for exploitation of the
physical environment by friendly forces.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         3-439                   Enclosure (1)
 3146                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L

body:
SERVICES 1. Introduction. The Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services OccFld is responsible for collecting, assessing, and disseminating environmental data, information, and intelligence, relevant to friendly and enemy force strengths and vulnerabilities for the planning and execution of operations necessary to characterize the battle space. This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices. The METOC OccFld is comprised of 6842 METOC Analyst Forecaster, 6891 METOC Chief, and 6802 METOC Services Officer. Marines entering the 6800 OccFld will complete formal training and receive MOS 6842. As their skill enhancing training progresses, they become eligible to attend MOSs 6852, 6862, and 6877 instruction.

4. MOS 6877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (MGySgt to SSgt) NMOS (6842), DC I a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Meteorology and Oceanography (METOC) Forecasters train personnel on environmental characterization and effects in relation to aviation operations in support of the MAGTF and aviation ground equipment, sensor, and weapon system performance in relation to enemy threats. WTI METOC Forecasters are proficient in the development of environmental sensing plans to characterize the physical environment and operational orders development required for designated staff billets. This MOS is assigned only as an NMOS to qualified METOC Forecasters. b. Prerequisites (1) Must hold MOS 6842. (2) Must complete aviation career progression model (ACPM) via Marine Net: (a) MAWTS8000X ACPM-8000 MACCS. (b) MAWTS8020X ACPM-8020 ACE. (c) MAWTS8040X ACPM-8040 Threat. (d) MAWTS8060X ACPM-8060 MAGTF. (e) MAWTS8080X ACPM-8080 Joint Air Operations. (3) Must hold the senior instructor (SI) designation per the MAWTS-1 Command, Control, and Communication (C3) Course Catalog. (4) Security requirement: must have a current single scope background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility. c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149721) Yuma, AZ. d. Duties (1) Management of local or subordinate METOC technical training programs. (2) Identify technical training shortfalls that prevent or hinder the development of METOC products in support of decision makers. (3) Develop or assist in the development of technical training that improves METOC support to decision makers. (4) Identify new or emerging METOC doctrinal support methods through Marine Corps Lesson Learned. (5) Develop or assist in the development of new METOC Tactics, Techniques & Procedures (TTPs) from Marine Corps Lessons Learned. (6) Develop the Annex H of a MAGTF or MSC operational order or plan to support Marine Corps, Joint, or Coalition operations in support of contingencies. (7) Develop MAGTF environmental collection plans that integrate with Joint Coalition environmental sensing strategies to support Marine Corps operations in support of contingencies. (8) Identify METOC sensitivities for MAGTF systems and operations to establish METOC thresholds to support all elements of the MAGTF by understanding the impact of the physical environment. (9) Identify METOC sensitivities for enemy systems and operations to establish METOC thresholds to determine opportunities for exploitation of the physical environment by friendly forces.

Compile and evaluate hydrologic information to prepare navigational charts and maps and to predict atmospheric conditions.
This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices.
Develop and deliver training on weather topics.

Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Meteorology and Oceanography (METOC) Forecasters train personnel on environmental characterization and effects in relation to aviation operations in support of the MAGTF and aviation ground equipment, sensor, and weapon system performance in relation to enemy threats.
Prepare personnel forecasts to project employment needs.

WTI METOC Forecasters are proficient in the development of environmental sensing plans to characterize the physical environment and operational orders development required for designated staff billets.
d. Duties (1) Management of local or subordinate METOC technical training programs.
Support the development of training materials and technical manuals.
(3) Develop or assist in the development of technical training that improves METOC support to decision makers.
Develop contingency plans to deal with emergencies.

Collaborate with environmental scientists, planners, hazardous waste technicians, engineers, experts in law or business, or other specialists to address environmental problems.
(7) Develop MAGTF environmental collection plans that integrate with Joint Coalition environmental sensing strategies to support Marine Corps operations in support of contingencies.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
